clue.text: Primate hot to a degree, wearing bearskin

indicators.note: the bearskin hat is worn around the other pieces, so it encloses them

parts.note: a busby is the tall fur hat of guardsmen, often called a bearskin
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
a BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a university degree

explanation.surface: A monkey wearing a guardsman's fur hat is getting rather warm.
explanation.definitionFit: The galago, a small nocturnal African primate with large eyes, is commonly called by this name.

clue.text: Strand into which runs gap

indicators.note: the runs letter goes into the beach word

parts.note: a strand is a shore or beach
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A beach with a gap that a stream runs into.
explanation.definitionFit: A breach is a gap or opening made in a wall or defence.

clue.text: Poser showing a bit of leg, getting softly squeezed before a kiss

indicators.note: the leg part comes first, ahead of the kiss
the softly letter is squashed inside the leg word

parts.note: the shin is part of the leg
p, piano, is the musical direction for softly
X is a kiss at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: A model flashing some leg, given a gentle squeeze and then a kiss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poser' suggests a model; it means one who poses riddles.
explanation.definitionFit: The mythical Greek creature set travellers a riddle, so it is a poser of puzzles.

clue.text: Dessert that may go off, did you say?

indicators.note: asks whether the word was heard spoken, signalling a sound-alike

parts.note: a bomb is something that may explode

explanation.surface: A pudding that might spoil, did you ask?
explanation.definitionFit: A frozen dome-shaped dessert, usually of ice cream, named after its rounded explosive shape.

clue.text: Good time to admit cardinal showing lack of interest

indicators.note: admitting lets something in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a boom is a time of prosperity
cardinal is a shade of red, as worn by cardinals

explanation.surface: A cardinal looking bored while invited to a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Tedium is the absence of interest, the state of weariness with nothing to engage you.

clue.text: Closely-related group on the fringes, heavily into Deep Purple

indicators.note: the edge letters of the next word go inside the colour word

parts.note: plum is a deep purple colour

indicators.note: fringes are outer edges, so take only the first and last letters of heavily

explanation.surface: Fans clustered around the edges, heavily into the rock band Deep Purple.
explanation.walkthrough: Deep Purple looks like the rock band but is just a colour; HY, the outer letters of 'heavily', go into PLUM.
explanation.definitionFit: In biological taxonomy, a phylum is a major rank grouping organisms sharing a basic body plan.

clue.text: Sting — a ruse created by a bee?

definitions.meaning: a covert operation to catch someone, especially by seduction

definitions.text: a ruse created by a bee?
definitions.meaning: literally a trap made of the sweet stuff bees produce

explanation.surface: A sting: is it a trick dreamt up by a bee?
explanation.definitionFit: A seduction-based trap used in espionage to compromise a target is a sting operation.

clue.text: Record describing revolutionary figure as Communist

indicators.note: to describe a shape is to draw around it, so the record word goes round

parts.note: a list is a record

indicators.note: revolving turns the figure word round backwards

parts.note: nine is a figure, a number

explanation.surface: A record portraying a revolutionary leader as a Communist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary figure' looks like a portrait of a rebel; it reverses NINE to ENIN, which LIST surrounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of the Russian Bolshevik leader's doctrine is a Marxist Communist.

clue.text: Waterbird chap assumes made us wet

indicators.note: to assume is to take on, so the chap word takes the other letters inside

parts.note: a chap is a man

indicators.note: made in the sense of formed into something new, so us wet is rearranged

explanation.surface: A man takes the blame for getting the group soaked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made us wet' reads as a soaking, but 'made' is the anagram signal for US WET, and 'assumes' puts the result (UTESW) inside the chap.
explanation.definitionFit: The common white swan of Europe, a large water bird.

clue.text: Those just passing time popping a concoction of hemp and ecstasy

indicators.note: the time word pops up beside the mixture, coming after it

parts.note: E is the slang abbreviation for the drug ecstasy

indicators.note: a concoction is a mixture, so the letters of hemp and E are stirred together

parts.note: an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Passers-by idle away time taking a cocktail of cannabis and ecstasy pills.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of HEMP plus E gives EPHEM, followed by ERA.
explanation.definitionFit: Ephemeral things last only briefly; the plural noun covers anything transitory, here people or things merely passing.

clue.text: Free junk, nothing to collect?

indicators.note: the letters are gathered from across the two words, sitting inside them

explanation.surface: An offer of free rubbish, with nothing to pay on collection.
explanation.definitionFit: To untie a knot in something is to release it, so the verb means set loose.

clue.text: Highest curve

definitions.meaning: chief or principal, as in a leading enemy
a curved shape or structure, as in a bridge

explanation.definitionFit: As a prefix or adjective it means chief; as a noun it is a curved structure.

clue.text: Hopeful political party, sore

parts.note: Con is short for Conservative, a UK political party
a sore spot is tender to the touch

explanation.surface: An aspiring politician, aggrieved with their own party.
explanation.definitionFit: A hopeful is a candidate with a chance of winning, which is what a contender is.

clue.text: That kiss is overlooked for a long time

parts.note: yon is an old or dialect word for that, as in yon hill

indicators.note: the letters of is are ignored and dropped from kiss

explanation.surface: A kiss that has been ignored for ages.
explanation.definitionFit: British informal slang for ages, a very long period, as in 'I haven't seen her for ages'.

clue.text: Something to take from tin to bin?

definitions.text: Something to take from tin to bin?

parts.words: Something to take from tin to bin?
parts.note: the tinned luncheon meat comes out of a can, while its namesake junk email gets sent to the bin folder

explanation.surface: Something you scoop out of a can and then throw away.
explanation.definitionFit: The tinned pork product shares its name with unwanted email, routinely deleted to the trash.

clue.text: As is a map lacking North, South, East and West?

definitions.text: As is a map lacking North, South, East and West?

parts.words: As is a map lacking North, South, East and West?
parts.note: the four compass points are missing, so the map is literally without its points

explanation.surface: A map with no compass bearings would be useless.
explanation.definitionFit: Meaning futile or useless, and literally without points of the compass.

clue.text: Eruption in rash is attributed to a pungent sauce

indicators.note: an eruption is a violent upheaval, so the letters of rash is get thrown about

explanation.surface: A spicy condiment is blamed for an outbreak of rash.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of RASHIS gives HARISS, then A is added.
explanation.definitionFit: A North African hot chilli paste, used as a fiery condiment and cooking sauce.

clue.text: One rushing to place hideous bottom on office equipment

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second
the bottom of a word is its last letter, here of hideous

parts.note: a printer is a standard piece of office equipment

explanation.surface: Someone hurrying to plonk their ugly backside on the photocopier.
explanation.definitionFit: An athlete who races short distances at top speed, someone dashing.

clue.text: Father accepting French writer was in control

indicators.note: accepting takes something in, so the writer goes inside

parts.note: God the Father
Jules Verne was a French novelist

explanation.surface: A priest taking in a French author who was in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruled or directed, past tense, matching the past-tense sense of having been in control.

clue.text: Punching nose, the last word in decency

indicators.note: punching through something puts a hole in it, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: to nose about is to pry
an obit, obituary, is the final word written about someone

explanation.surface: Hitting someone on the nose: the ultimate in good manners.
explanation.definitionFit: Probity is uprightness and honesty, the quality of moral decency.

clue.text: Enclosed area, not far?

definitions.meaning: a courtyard or fenced patch of ground
three feet is a small distance, hardly far

explanation.definitionFit: An enclosure beside a building, and also a short unit of length.

clue.text: Promotion of worthy people

indicators.note: the letters are taken from within the words worthy people

explanation.surface: Advancement of deserving people at work.
explanation.definitionFit: Publicity puffing something up is a form of promotion, as in media hype.

clue.text: Acre in empty land

indicators.note: the acre letter goes inside the empty word

parts.note: an empty stomach is hungry

explanation.surface: An acre of barren territory.
explanation.definitionFit: A Central European country, a land or nation.

clue.text: Extra room where queen accommodates old lover

indicators.note: accommodating gives room inside, so the old lover goes in

parts.note: Anne was a Queen of Great Britain
an ex is a former partner

explanation.surface: The spare room where the queen puts up her ex.
explanation.definitionFit: A building or room added on to a main building as an extension.

clue.text: Lovely to transport oxygen through the blood vessels

definitions.note: a noun phrase defining an adjective meaning of the veins

indicators.note: transporting carries something, so the lovely word holds the oxygen letter

parts.note: Venus is the goddess of beauty, or a lovely woman
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: Something beautiful carrying oxygen around the bloodstream.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes the veins, the vessels returning blood to the heart.

clue.text: Maladroit in record time!

parts.note: an EP, extended play, is a type of record

explanation.surface: Someone clumsy who nonetheless finishes in record time.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean clumsy and unskilled, lacking competence.

clue.text: Set money aside for criminal going after gang

indicators.note: the criminal word follows the gang word

parts.note: a ring is a criminal gang, as in a drugs ring
a fence is a criminal who handles stolen goods

explanation.surface: A crook pursuing a gang to get money stashed away for something.
explanation.definitionFit: To protect funds by earmarking them for one purpose only is the financial sense of this verb.

clue.text: Sweet stall

definitions.meaning: a soft confection made of sugar, butter and milk
to evade or play for time by being vague

explanation.definitionFit: A soft sugary confection, and a verb meaning to dodge or delay.

clue.text: Note musician sounded

indicators.note: the musician's word is spoken out loud, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: a tenor is a singer, a musician

explanation.surface: A musician sounded a note.
explanation.definitionFit: A ten-pound note in British slang, a banknote, which is what the clue word means here.

clue.text: Characters from central Helsinki travel beyond eastern US city

indicators.note: the travel word comes after the eastern letter

parts.note: the central characters of Helsinki are S and I, spelled out with the joining word
to go is to travel

explanation.surface: A traveller heading past eastern Finland's capital towards an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: The two middle letters of HELSINKI are S and I, written in full as the phrase S AND I.
explanation.definitionFit: A large Californian city on the Pacific coast near Mexico.

clue.text: Salad ingredient is hard to misspell

indicators.note: misspelling puts letters in the wrong order, so is hard is rearranged

explanation.surface: A salad vegetable whose name is difficult to spell.
explanation.definitionFit: A crunchy red root vegetable often sliced into salads.

clue.text: Pacifying youth leaders, extraordinarily serene mountains

indicators.note: the leaders of words are their first letters
something done extraordinarily is out of the ordinary, so serene is rearranged

explanation.surface: Calming the young, the mountains are remarkably peaceful.
explanation.definitionFit: A range of mountains forming the border between France and Spain.
